extracted.intended_audience: readers of NoTricksZone; climate skeptics and media-criticism audience
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing mainstream journalism for credibility, accuracy, ideological bias, balance, and editorial oversight—with a focus on climate reporting and German/Western media. The page argues criteria by negative example (the Relotius fabrications) and broader claims about institutional bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy / no fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: “one of its star reporters had been fabricating stories for years.” / “The extent of the news fabrication is no better illustrated than in the case of Fergus Falls, Minnesota, where now disgraced journalist Claas Relotius invented stories.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat fabrication as a fatal flaw; fact-check stories (e.g., the Fergus Falls piece) and look for invented details. Anti-patterns: invented anecdotes, quoted people who don't exist, claims a child could refute with a Google search. Use examples of Relotius as a negative exemplar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and fact-checking responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “How could this have gotten by Spiegel editors?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the strength of editorial checks and fact-verification processes. A credible outlet should explain how systemic failures occurred and demonstrate concrete changes. Lack of explanation or shrugging it off as isolated error suggests weak oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and avoidance of one-sided reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: “one-sided, distorted activist news reports” / “In this one-sided hit piece, Blasberg and Kohlenberg relied solely on carefully selected ‘facts’ to tailor a narrative.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporting presents multiple sides and avoids tailoring facts to fit a preconceived narrative. Anti-patterns: presenting a single perspective as the whole story, omission of relevant counter-evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding stereotyping and malicious smearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Relotius allegedly “viciously smearing rural American Trump voters as contemptible, small-minded, gun-toting, right-wing religious rednecks.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good journalism avoids derogatory, blanket characterizations of groups. Check for unfair caricatures or language intended to denigrate rather than inform; such stereotyping indicates poor ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of dissenting viewpoints / not censoring skeptics
rubrics_metrics.description: “both the BBC and LA Times have declared not to provide a forum to climate skeptics.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether an outlet provides forum space for legitimate dissenting views (e.g., climate skeptics) rather than excluding them outright. Anti-patterns: formal policies or editorial practice that refuse to publish contrary perspectives without substantive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding cherry-picking and half-truths
rubrics_metrics.description: “they are fully engaged in one-sided journalism and half-truths” / “relied solely on carefully selected ‘facts’ to tailor a narrative.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether evidence is presented in full context or selectively chosen to support a narrative. Look for omitted facts, misleading emphasis, or selective timelines that distort understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/ideological impartiality (avoid partisan framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Relotius is only the tip of the overall sentiment in a leftist newsroom that has long despised the American conservative heartland.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether reporting is influenced by institutional political sympathies. Indicators of bias include habitual framing that favors one political perspective and repeated derogatory portrayals of the opposing side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate representation of opponents’ views (no mislabeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The fact however is that 1) climate science skeptics don’t deny climate change, 2) they agree that man has an impact on climate, but in a more modest way and 3) skeptics don’t believe it is a crisis to humanity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting fairly and accurately summarizes the positions of those it critiques rather than using straw-man labels like 'denier.' Mischaracterization is a sign of poor reporting and rhetorical bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accountability and transparent response to scandal
rubrics_metrics.description: “The strategy so far appears to be to make Relotius look as if he was just an isolated renegade … and now Spiegel is moving quickly and decisively!” / “It’s doubtful Spiegel whether will ever recover its credibility…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the outlet accepts systemic responsibility, publishes transparent investigations, and implements reforms. Merely portraying misconduct as isolated without evidence of reform undermines trust. Credibility recovery requires substantive corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of reporting from editorial preferences / avoid pandering
rubrics_metrics.description: “he told Spiegel editors exactly what appealed to them.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporters tailor stories to match perceived editorial tastes rather than follow independent evidence. Independence implies reporters present findings even if they conflict with editors’ ideological preferences; pandering is an anti-pattern.
